what_this_is: A worksheet, not a report. Fifteen riders and one card; each feature is one finding. The coordinates are NOT a place on the ground - there is none, and inventing one is the thing this estate refuses. They are the Kuiper's own arrangement, golden angle, r = sqrt(k), which is how the archive lays out anything without a real position.
how_to_read: verified: self = I saw it; agent = a rider claimed it and I have not checked; both = claimed and confirmed; contradicted = claimed and wrong. A finding that cannot say which is a rumour, so there is no default. crunchable = the card can settle it without anyone reading anything.
contradicted_are_kept: Four claims did not survive checking, and they stay on the sheet. A rider being wrong is data about the race, and deleting it would make the next sheet look more reliable than it is.
anonymised: No project, site, client, maker or model anywhere.

properties.what: A verdict returned a PASS on a value that is not a number: `v > limit` is false for NaN, so the card read 'inside the 1500 V rating by NaN V'.
properties.evidence: 8,000,132 checks on the card: 0 disagreements on any finite number, 1,001,580 where the old form passes what it cannot justify.
properties.fix: over = !(x <= limit), plus a guard that refuses and draws nothing.

properties.what: An unknown module class silently became the 660 W bin, and a typo in an input KEY was ignored while its default answered in its place.
properties.evidence: Refusal verified on four bad inputs; three good inputs return byte-identical answers.
properties.fix: A key-walk guard: refuse by name, list what would be accepted.

properties.what: Four places rebuilt a drawing from a name table instead of taking it from the program that made it. One failed silently: null body, correct numbers on the card, nothing drawn.
properties.where: sldLayout, makeSldBody, the colouring, the fired command
properties.evidence: Watched it fail, patched it, watched it draw.
properties.fix: Each now believes a program that hands over finished pieces.

properties.what: sldLayout picks SYMBOLS by a PREFIX match on 'pv'. 32 comb pieces claimed 32 symbol floors - 704 of 896 dots - and the collection busbar, the spine of the drawing, silently did not appear.
properties.evidence: Seen on screen: blocks hanging off nothing, every number correct.
properties.fix: Tag repeated pieces with a non-symbol prefix. A dot-budget gate is written and not yet wired.

properties.what: The text window was pinned to screen centre, which is exactly where the disc is, so every drawing was read through the thing describing it.
properties.evidence: 271,499,532 viewport configurations swept: the proposed furniture crowds the dots less, 54.1M against 64.6M.
properties.fix: Docked right. The full workspace spec is written and not applied.

properties.what: The reader's Kuiper at /kuiper/ does not contain the site, block, network or string programs AT ALL. The whole plant-drawing body of work is only reachable behind a page marked DEVELOPMENT ENVIRONMENT.
properties.evidence: Fetched and hashed: /kuiper/ serves k0036 programs, 17,738 bytes; the head is k0093 at 328,185 bytes. Not a fork - all 11 of its cartridges exist byte-identically in the head.
properties.fix: Promote by pointer, do not port file by file. Pick the NEWEST cartridge per slot - the head selects an older chrome and tests.

properties.what: The whole result tile is a block <a target=_blank> with no affordance, and #card is fixed over a command bar that lives in normal flow. A tap meant for the bar lands on the anchor, focus goes to the link, and every keystroke after it is lost.
properties.evidence: Two defects with one root cause; reproduced by CSS geometry, not by a captured keystroke loss.
properties.fix: Only the OPEN control is a link; the tile becomes a div.

properties.what: The shell breaks at 640px and the cartridge at 700px, so 641-700px is a band where the two layouts disagree.
properties.evidence: One rider called narrow() the load-bearing edit; a second refuted that, finding kuiper-chrome.js already matches at 640.
properties.fix: Unify on 700, both files, including narrow().

properties.what: Collapsing the foot breaks shipped self-tests, and the escape hatch that would save one is ALREADY DEAD: the test asks for #appschip, the cartridge creates #chipapps.
properties.where: kuiper-tests.js T26, phoneSelftest T9, isolateSelftest T1
properties.evidence: A 3-minute rider refuted a 6-minute rider's first claim and found a failure it had missed.
properties.fix: One id and one breakpoint. Do not hide the warranty line - it is what two of those tests protect.

properties.what: No night-results file carries a `schema` field. A counter reading one key instead of another already understated a published total by 79.9%.
properties.evidence: 13,901,209,740,000 cases logged as a success worth nothing.
properties.fix: A schema string per file, and a reader that refuses rather than defaults.

properties.what: The deploy path list is an allow-list that has been wrong five times. i0092 was pushed, gated, hashed and merged while the live site served i0091, with nothing red anywhere.
properties.evidence: The file's own comments were already counting: third time, fourth time. This was the fifth.
properties.fix: kuiper-grid/** added. Invert to paths-ignore - that is a decision about the runners, not a typo.

properties.what: The public language gate had been failing for days on a missing file: all twelve runner workspaces were left sparse by an earlier job, so it checked no language at all while looking like a wording failure.
properties.evidence: Clearing the config alone did not fix it - three things make a tree sparse and the index's skip-worktree bit is the one that actually hides files.
properties.fix: Guard clears all three before checkout; a step now says 'could not run' in those words.

properties.what: CuPy is not importable from the machine's default python, so a GPU gate wired to it would go green by absence - exactly the failure the language gate spent days in.
properties.evidence: python -c 'import cupy' fails; the venv at E:/swarm/gpu-bench/venv has it.
properties.fix: Point CI at the venv python, and keep the 'could not run' step.

properties.what: Claimed: `fire block {}` draws nothing on the new build.
properties.evidence: Tested on both builds with the console listener attached BEFORE load: draws identically on i0091 and i0092, zero console errors. A small viewport and a screenshot taken before the dots settle.
properties.fix: None. The reasoning that the patch could not touch block was right, and the evidence agreed.

properties.what: Claimed: at the sheet's top rear row the current is still inside its limits.
properties.evidence: At 25% rear EVERY class breaches BOTH current tests. The machine input turns at 13.60% - a tenth of a point above the 13.5% the datasheet itself publishes.
properties.fix: Cut from the set. It was ranked in a kept top half, and it is a 'we checked and it is fine' that the numbers call a breach.

properties.what: Claimed: the higher-Voc family swap works at 28 modules.
properties.evidence: 1523.78 V at -10 C, over by 23.78 V; its turn is -2.36 C. The swap needs 27.
properties.fix: Corrected to 27. Shipping 28 would have put an over-voltage string in front of a reader as the safe answer.

properties.what: Claimed: the site drawing is a frozen unlabelled field, not a site.
properties.evidence: I watched this render and published it: grid, interface, transformer, collection busbar, eight block columns. The colour is the amber over-rating verdict at close zoom, which is the drawing working.
properties.fix: None. Kept because a rider being wrong is data about the race.

properties.what: Claimed: the shell loads a 15 KB programs file, so the workspace patch is two patches that cannot be pasted into one page.
properties.evidence: That is the RAW shell. The composer's replace-script slot swaps it by filename at load. I read FIRE_SLD_KIND on the live page and it contains 'site', which exists only in the cartridge.
properties.fix: None, but the rest of that report stands and is worth keeping.

properties.what: My overnight counter read one key, `cases`. One sweep writes `space`. It ran 47 times, verified itself every time, and was logged as a SUCCESS contributing nothing.
properties.evidence: Understated the published total by 79.9%: 17.39tn reported against 31.29tn actual.
properties.fix: Reads cases, then evaluated, then space; refuses outright if it finds none.

properties.what: My ranking rule for worked examples was degenerate: series count does not enter the current tests, so ranking by the current crossing returned the same row fifteen times.
properties.evidence: The card found the right numbers and was asked the wrong question. The riders' selections were better than mine.
properties.fix: Require each example to teach a DIFFERENT thing; dedupe on which test turns.

properties.what: worked_examples.py defines SIZING = 1.25 and never uses it, so its string-input margin is optimistic against any Isc convention.
properties.evidence: Found by the arbiter reading my own file.
properties.fix: Either apply it to a cable/OCPD test or delete it and say so.

properties.what: My layout gate's absolute crowding counts are an upper bound, not a prediction: it sizes a dot from zoom alone while the renderer sizes it from measured spacing.
properties.evidence: The comparison survives the limitation; the absolute number does not.
properties.fix: Model bodyDotPx() properly, or keep reporting only the comparison.
